title: Two-dimensional sandpile prediction in NC
formal: Is the following decision problem in logspace-uniform NC? An input gives positive integers W,H, an explicit W-by-H array c with entries in \(\{0,1,2,3\}\), and two cells p,q in that rectangle. Extend c by zero to the whole integer square lattice and add one grain at p. Answer YES exactly when q eventually topples under the four-neighbor parallel sandpile dynamics defined below. The input length N includes every array entry, not a compressed representation.
definitions: The four neighbor displacements are \(E=\{(1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)\}\). Set \(c_{0}(v)=c(v)+1\) if \(v=p\), and \(c_{0}(v)=c(v)\) otherwise. At each integer time \(t\ge 0\) every vertex v with \(c_{t}(v)\ge 4\) topples once, losing four grains and sending one to each neighbor. Equivalently, \(c_{t+1}(v)=c_{t}(v)-4 I[c_{t}(v)\ge 4]+\sum\)_{e in E} \(I[c_{t}(v-e)\ge 4]\), where I is the indicator. The question is whether \(c_{t}(q)\ge 4\) for some \(t\ge 0\). The array is row-major with binary dimensions and cell coordinates; invalid encodings are rejected. The zero extension is an infinite lattice, not a periodic boundary or a boundary that absorbs grains. A supplied rectangle may contain extra zero rows or columns to include p and q. Finite initial mass eventually stabilizes. NC here means that for some fixed integers a,k the decision has Boolean circuits of size \(O(N^{a})\) and depth \(O((\log  N)^{k})\), with fan-in at most two, whose description is generated from \(1^{N}\) in \(O(\log  N)\) work space. There is no requested time t in the input and the answer is exact, without random error.
answer_criterion: Prove or refute membership of the specified language in logspace-uniform NC. Any complexity assumption used in a negative result must be stated explicitly.
why: A local deterministic physical process can have a long cascade after a single perturbation. This problem asks whether its outcome permits an efficient parallel computation, addressing the boundary between prediction and sequential evolution.

importance.reason: A canonical unresolved parallel-complexity question for a simple two-dimensional dynamical system, connecting computational prediction with statistical physics.

context_blocks.text: The initial configuration is stable, so all activity comes from the extra grain. The requested output is a single eventual-toppling bit; computing the entire final configuration or a toppling at a specified time are related but different tasks.
The classical dimension-dependent results provide efficient parallel prediction in one dimension and P-completeness in dimensions at least three. They leave the planar case as a distinct question.

Recent work still separates the standard four-neighbor lattice from weighted or nonuniform grids. NC membership and P-completeness are not an unconditional exclusive dichotomy: a P-completeness result rules out NC only under \(\mathrm{NC} \ne  \mathrm{P}\).

progress.text: Moore and Nilsson obtain \(\mathrm{NC}^{3}\) prediction in one dimension and P-completeness in dimensions at least three, leaving dimension two open.
Concha-Vega and Perrot explicitly define single-grain eventual prediction on the infinite lattice and retain the von Neumann-neighborhood problem as open.
A new preprint studies weighted and nonuniform crossing constructions and continues to state the standard two-dimensional complexity question as open.
